intro.line: Far from Dominaria, a plane made entirely of metal. Karn built it, called it Argentum, and left.
He left a keeper behind: a golem named Memnarch. Memnarch kept the plane for a very long time, alone.
In the blur between metal and flesh, Memnarch found madness.
Now the plane is called Mirrodin. Four suns cross its sky. Elves, leonin, goblins and men live on it, and none of them know how they got here.
There's a secret at the heart of this world, and I will unlock it.

finale.line: In the Panopticon, Memnarch falls. The keeper of Mirrodin goes still among his myr.
He was going to cut the spark out of me. Whatever a spark is.
Something old. Something he wanted to be. Slobad thinks he copied it from somebody.
The ur-golem etchings begin by celebrating Mirrodin's creator, a golem of almost limitless power. They end by cursing its protector, a being called Memnarch.
The levelers stop. The myr stop watching. Five suns cross the sky now, and the Tangle grows toward the green one.
Deep in the core, where nobody looks, a drop of black oil that was never part of Karn's design begins, very slowly, to spread.

villainFinale.line: The elf lies still on the floor of the Panopticon. Memnarch bends over her, listening for the spark.
I was built to keep his world. He never came back to see it.
So I kept it. I made the myr and the levelers. Everything he made, I made again.
And now I will take the one thing he had that I did not. Then I will leave, as he did.
Deep in the core, a drop of black oil moves. Memnarch does not notice. He never did.

battles.title: Glissa's Hunt
battles.blurb: The levelers came through the Tangle and killed Glissa's family. Every elf says they come once a century, from nowhere, for no reason. Glissa does not believe in no reason.

scene.line: Once a century, the levelers rip through every corner of Mirrodin, obeying the commands of an unseen master.
When the levelers come again, we shall be ready for them.
Equipment: pay once to make it, then pay its equip cost to strap it to a creature. If the creature dies, the blade stays. Pick it up again.
They are machines. Machines have makers. I want to know who.

villainScene.line: The levelers do not speak. Somewhere above the Tangle, something is counting.
Memnarch created the myr with three qualities in mind: dependability, controllability, and disposability.

after.line: This one carried a mark. Not elf work. Not goblin. Someone built these on purpose.
A goblin is picking through the wreck before the smoke clears.

hero.start: For my mother. For my father.
hero.low: There are too many of them...
hero.win: Machines have makers. I will find yours.

battles.title: Junk into Engines
battles.blurb: Slobad was thrown out of the Krark Clan for being too clever. He knows artifacts better than anyone in the Tangle, and he has just been caught by vedalken hoverguards taking one apart.

scene.line: The vedalken interrogate all intruders, once the hoverguards are done with them.
Is it the stomping kind or the munching kind?
Affinity: every artifact you have makes affinity spells cost one less. Artifact lands count too. Pile up junk, and the big ones cost nothing.
Can you fight?
No. But the junk can.

villainScene.line: It could be made to run silently, but its low hum reminds the Neurok that they are always watched.
Vedalken eyes don't see the beauty in things. They see only what those things can teach.
Goblin. Elf. Both off their maps. Report to the Synod.

after.line: I used to joke that he had been exiled for being too smart. Now I know why he never laughed.

hero.loss: Slobad should have stayed in the Furnace...

battles.title: Stored in the Machine
battles.blurb: In the vedalken city of Lumengrid, the researcher Pontifex keeps a vault of machines that remember. An iron golem has walked in looking for his own past. Pontifex would like to keep him.

scene.line: As Glissa searches for the truth about Memnarch, Bosh searches to unearth the secrets of his past.
This machine. It has my face inside it.
Imprint: some machines exile a card when they arrive, and keep it. Duplicant becomes the creature it ate. Mirror Golem guards against everything it holds.
So if it eats Bosh, it becomes Bosh?
Precisely. Isn't it wonderful?

villainScene.line: Did it have this shape upon Mirrodin's creation, or did some inconceivable force shape the unshapable?
A golem that thinks. I must have him for the archive.

after.line: The machine showed me a forge. Older than this world. And a maker, walking away.

battles.title: Darksteel
battles.blurb: Under the plane's surface, Memnarch's Arcbound crews guard the way to his tower. They take each other apart to grow, and the darksteel they stand on cannot be broken.

scene.line: Panopticon, forge of the Darksteel Eye, home of Mirrodin's keeper.
Darksteel. Nothing breaks it. Slobad tried for a whole year.
Modular: when an Arcbound dies, its counters jump to another artifact creature. Kill the Ravager first, or every death feeds it.
The parts are as strong as the whole.

villainScene.line: Break in case of emergency.
[the crew locks together, plate to plate]

after.line: At the bottom of the shaft, a tower of darksteel. On it, an eye that never closes.

battles.title: The Fifth Dawn
battles.blurb: A fifth sun is rising out of Mirrodin's core. Raksha, the young leonin kha, takes it as a sign. So does Geth, keeper of the Vault, and his nim come out of the Mephidross to meet it.

scene.line: To some the birth of the fifth sun was a sign of doom. To others it was a sign of salvation. But to all it was a sign.
I may be kha, but without my soldiers, my people, I am nothing.
Sunburst: these machines take a counter for each colour of mana spent on them. Pay with every colour you have.
A chorus of life heralds the arrival of Mirrodin's final sun.

villainScene.line: Feel the burn of the mists. Master them. They will devour your enemies.
In the swirling mists, you could walk right up to one and not know until its teeth are in your throat.
The one who dies with the most toys is still dead.

after.line: The fifth sun clears the horizon. It is green. In the Tangle, every tree turns toward it.

hero.win: The nim go back to the Dross.

battles.title: Ravager Affinity
battles.blurb: Around the real world in 2004, one deck was everywhere: Arcbound Ravager and a pile of artifact lands. On Mirrodin, the Krark Clan built the same thing out of scrap. You get the original.

scene.line: All the junk, refuse, and offal of the Krark Clan is diligently collected, melted down, and made into more junk, refuse, and offal.
A mirror. Same engine, different paint.
Feed the Ravager what is about to die anyway. Never feed it a land you still need.
From trinket to trauma.

villainScene.line: What do you mean, we're out of stuff to melt down? Give me your leg.
Well, I jammed the whatsit into the whackdoodle, but I think I broke the thingamajigger.

battles.title: Tooth and Nail
battles.blurb: The Sylvok druids grow mana out of the Tangle until they can call anything. Janus of the vedalken Synod holds the shackles that let him take anything. Two ways to win a long game.

scene.line: Any creature on a druid's shoulder is his family, any land under his feet his home.
He watches from above. He watches from below. He watches from within.
Entwine: a spell with two modes. Pay the entwine cost and you get both. Tooth and Nail with nine mana finds two creatures and puts them into play.

villainScene.line: The Knowledge Pool knows. Memnarch understands.
Memnarch shared a touch of his power with the vedalken in return for their service. It is a debt he intends to collect.

hero.loss: The roots... were not deep enough...

battles.title: Memnarch
battles.blurb: Memnarch made the levelers and the myr, all to pull one elf to his tower. Glissa has a spark, and he wants it. Glissa, Slobad and Bosh go to the Panopticon to end it.

scene.line: It is all in my grasp. Every petty dream, every grand scheme, every soul, every fear. It all flows through me and from me.
You killed my family to bring me here.
If only the living were so easily salvaged.
He takes things. Shackles take your creatures, Memnarch takes your machines. Keep your best one back until his tricks are spent.

villainScene.line: Secrets are meant to remain secret.
The elf carries a spark. My maker had one. With it, he left. With it, I will follow.
Perhaps I should take Mirrodin apart and begin again.

hero.start: For the Tangle. For everyone you harvested.
hero.loss: The spark... he is taking it...

half.line: He copied everything his maker did. Slobad thinks he never knew how to be anything else.

battles.title: Clamped
battles.blurb: Deep in the Vault, a deck that broke a whole season. Every creature you kill draws it two cards.

archive.format: Standard: Onslaught block, Eighth Edition, Mirrodin and Darksteel.
archive.what: Ravager Affinity with Skullclamp, the one-mana equipment from Darksteel. Put it on a 1-toughness creature, the creature dies, you draw two cards.
archive.why: Every cheap artifact creature turned into two cards, and Arcbound Ravager and Disciple of the Vault turned every death into damage. It ran out of cards almost never.
archive.beat: Kill the Skullclamp, not the creatures. Without it they are only small machines. Hit the artifact lands and the deck slows to a crawl.
archive.after: Skullclamp was banned in Standard from 20 June 2004. The rest of the deck kept winning until March 2005, when Arcbound Ravager, Disciple of the Vault and every artifact land were banned too.

deck.name: Skullclamp Affinity
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from the spring 2004 Ravager Affinity lists, with Skullclamp before its ban. No single tournament list is copied.

scene.line: The archive opens on a deck from a single season. Its first card is a small black bone clamp.
Every death draws it two cards. Then I stop killing the creatures.
Slobad would break the clamp. Then everything else.

villainScene.line: The deck does not speak. It draws.

after.line: Recorded: banned 20 June 2004. One of the shortest lives a common equipment ever had.

hero.loss: Two more cards. Always two more.
